title: Cut and trim clips on the Edit page
summary: Split a clip at the playhead, remove a piece without leaving a gap, and trim a clip end.

steps.say: Click Edit on the bottom bar of the window to open the Edit page.

checks.prompt: Is the Edit page active, with the Edit icon highlighted on the bottom bar and a timeline across the lower part of the window?

hints: The page buttons are icons with labels in a row along the very bottom edge. Edit is one of them.
You can also press Shift 4 to jump straight to the Edit page.
steps.why: Every task in Resolve belongs to a page, and the Edit page has the tools for this lesson.

steps.say: Press A to make sure the Selection tool is active.

checks.prompt: Is the arrow Selection tool highlighted in the timeline toolbar?

hints: Click once on an empty part of the timeline first so the key goes to the timeline.
You can also click the arrow icon in the toolbar above the timeline.
steps.why: The Selection tool lets you click and move clips without cutting them.

steps.say: Click in the time ruler above the tracks where you want to cut.

check.prompt: Has the red playhead line moved to a new position in the timeline?

hints: The ruler is the strip with timecode numbers along the top of the timeline.
Press Space to play and Space again to stop at the moment you want.
steps.why: Resolve cuts at the playhead, so its position decides where the split happens.

steps.say: Press Control B to cut the clip at the playhead.

checks.prompt: Is there a new cut line splitting the clip exactly under the playhead?

hints: Hold Control and tap B. The clip under the red line splits into two pieces.
You can also press B for the Blade tool and click on the clip, then press A to go back.
steps.why: Cutting splits one clip into two so you can remove or move a part of it.

steps.say: Click the piece of the clip you want to remove.

check.prompt: Is one part of the cut clip now outlined in red or orange as selected?

hints: A selected clip gets a coloured outline. Click once, without dragging.
If both sides highlight, click an empty area first and then click only one piece.
steps.why: Resolve only deletes what is selected, so pick the part you do not want.

steps.say: Press Shift Backspace to delete it and close the gap. Control Z undoes it.

checks.prompt: Has the selected piece disappeared with the following clips moved left to close the gap?

hints: Plain Backspace leaves an empty gap. Add Shift to slide the later clips over.
You can also right click the clip and choose Ripple Delete.
steps.why: Ripple delete keeps your edit tight, with no black gaps between clips.

steps.say: Press T to switch to Trim Edit mode.

checks.prompt: Is the Trim Edit mode button highlighted in the timeline toolbar?

hints: The Trim button is next to the arrow in the toolbar above the timeline.
Click the timeline first if the key does nothing, then press T again.
steps.why: Trim mode lets you change where clips start and end while keeping neighbours in place.

steps.say: Drag the right edge of a clip to the left to shorten it.

check.prompt: Is one of the clips in the timeline shorter than before?

hints: Move the mouse onto the right edge of a clip until the pointer changes, then drag left.
Press Control Z if you trimmed the wrong clip.
steps.why: Trimming removes slow starts and ends so the video keeps moving.

steps.say: Press A to go back to the Selection tool.

checks.prompt: Is the arrow Selection tool highlighted again?

hints: A is the shortcut for the arrow tool in the timeline toolbar.
You can click the arrow icon above the timeline instead.
steps.why: Returning to the Selection tool prevents accidental trims while you keep working.
